1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to ANY AGENTS when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	AutoRound — post-training quantization for LLMs/VLMs using sign-gradient descent. Publishes as `auto-round` (GPU/CPU) and `auto-round-hpu` (Intel Gaudi).
8	
9	## Build & Install
10	
11	```bash
12	# From source (GPU/CPU) — --no-build-isolation is required when PyTorch is already installed
13	pip install --no-build-isolation -e .
14	
15	# HPU variant
16	BUILD_HPU_ONLY=1 pip install --no-build-isolation .
17	# or: python setup.py hpu install
18	
19	# XPU variant — install Intel PyTorch first
20	pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu
21	pip install --no-build-isolation .
22	```
23	
24	## Testing
25	
26	Tests are split into three tiers under `test/`: `unit/` (fast, runs in PR CI),
27	`integration/` (third-party frameworks, runs nightly), and `e2e/` (full models /
28	real inference engines, runs weekly). Each tier is further split by hardware
29	(`test_cpu/`, `test_cuda/`, `test_hpu/`, `test_xpu/`, `test_ark/`, `test_mlx/`).
30	
31	```bash
32	# CPU unit tests (most common during development)
33	pytest test/unit/test_cpu/ -x -q
34	
35	# Single test
36	pytest test/unit/test_cpu/ -k "test_name" -x -q
37	
38	# Hardware-specific unit tests
39	pytest test/unit/test_cuda/
40	pytest test/unit/test_hpu/ --mode=lazy   # or --mode=compile
41	pytest test/unit/test_xpu/
42	
43	# Slower suites (nightly / weekly)
44	pytest test/integration/test_cpu/
45	pytest test/e2e/test_cpu/
46	```
47	
48	Test fixtures create tiny models (OPT-125M, Qwen-0.6B) at session scope — first run downloads them.
49	
50	## Code Style
51	
52	- **Line length: 120** (non-default) — enforced by black, isort, ruff, pylint
53	- **Formatter: black** (profile used by isort)
54	- **Import sorting: isort** with `profile=black`, first-party: `auto_round`, `auto_round_extension`
55	- **Linter: ruff** — rules `E4, E7, E9, F, NPY, FURB`; E501/E402/F401/F403 are intentionally ignored
56	- **License header**: Apache 2.0 auto-inserted into `.py/.yaml/.yml/.sh` under `auto_round/` and `auto_round_extension/`
57	- Pre-commit config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
58	
59	## Commit & PR Conventions
60	
61	- Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`
62	- PRs target `main`, squash-merged
63	- **CN docs rule**: any change to a `.md` file must include a matching update to its `_CN` counterpart (e.g., `README.md` → `README_CN.md`)
64	
65	## Key Environment Variables
66	
67	- `BUILD_HPU_ONLY=1` — build HPU package variant
68	- `AR_USE_MODELSCOPE=1` — use ModelScope instead of HuggingFace for model downloads
69	- `FORCE_BF16=1` — force BF16 in tests (used in CI)
70	
71	## Source Layout
72	
73	- `auto_round/` — core library (AutoRound class, sign-SGD, exporters, eval, data types)
74	- `auto_round_extension/` — hardware backends (CUDA, HPU, IPEX/XPU, Triton, ARK, vLLM)
75	- `test/` — tests organized by tier then hardware: `unit/` (PR CI), `integration/` (nightly), `e2e/` (weekly), each with `test_cpu/`, `test_cuda/`, ...
76	- `examples/` — usage examples for different model types
77	
78	## Gotchas
79	
80	- `setup.py` forces `CC=CXX=g++` at import time
81	- Version is computed dynamically from git tags — untagged commits produce dev versions
82	- Some test dependencies (AutoAWQ, GPTQModel, llama-cpp) require manual git installs — see comments in `test/unit/test_cuda/requirements.txt`

57	    name: str,
58	    *,
59	    aliases: tuple[str, ...] = (),
60	    config_factory: Callable[[], object] | None = None,
61	    cli_handler: type | None = None,
62	    summary: str = "",

64	) -> None:

66	    entry = _ALG_REGISTRY.get(key)

72	        dict.fromkeys((entry.aliases or ()) + tuple(a.strip().lower() for a in aliases if a.strip()))

74	    if config_factory is not None:
75	        entry.config_factory = config_factory

82	    entry.aliases = merged_aliases

94	def resolve_algorithm_names(algorithms, *, ignore_unknown: bool = False) -> list[str]:
95	    """Resolve one algorithm string or sequence to ordered canonical names.
96	
97	    A comma-separated string and a sequence use exactly the same semantics.
98	    Duplicate aliases are removed while preserving the first occurrence.
99	    """
100	    if isinstance(algorithms, str):
101	        raw_names = algorithms.split(",")
102	    else:
103	        raw_names = list(algorithms)
104	
105	    canonical_names = []
106	    seen = set()
107	    for raw_name in raw_names:
108	        if not isinstance(raw_name, str):
109	            raise TypeError(f"Algorithm names must be strings, got {type(raw_name).__name__}.")
110	        name = raw_name.strip()
111	        if not name:
112	            continue
113	        canonical = resolve_algorithm_alias(name)
114	        if canonical is None:
115	            if ignore_unknown:
116	                continue
117	            supported_aliases = sorted(_ALIAS_TO_NAME.keys())
118	            raise ValueError(
119	                f"Unknown algorithm alias '{name}'. Supported aliases: {supported_aliases}. "
120	                "If you are adding a new algorithm, register it via "
121	                "auto_round.algorithms.registry.register_algorithm()."
122	            )
123	        if canonical not in seen:
124	            canonical_names.append(canonical)
125	            seen.add(canonical)
126	    return canonical_names

14	"""Algorithm Fusion Pipeline abstraction.
15	
16	This module defines the core data structures and utilities for composing
17	pre-processing algorithms (AWQ smooth, SmoothQuant, Rotation…) with a
18	block-quantization algorithm (RTN, SignRound/AutoRound…) into a single
19	shared-calibration bundle.
20	
21	Design invariants (see AWQ_REFACTOR_PLAN.md §0.0 and §3.0):
22	- ``AlgorithmComposer`` is the *first-class abstraction*; it is NOT just
23	  AWQ's helper.
24	- All block-wise scheduling in ``Compressor`` operates against
25	  ``AlgorithmComposer``, never against a concrete ``AWQTransform``.
26	- Single-algorithm use is expressed as
27	  ``AlgorithmComposer(preprocessors=[], block_quantizer=q)``, which is
28	  semantically identical to the current direct-quantizer path.
29	"""
30

32

34	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

40	    get_algorithm_class,

59	@dataclass
60	class BlockContext:
61	    """Per-block context threaded through the lifecycle hooks.
62	
63	    Passed to lifecycle methods like ``block_forward_hooks``,
64	    ``pre_quantize_block``, ``post_quantize_block``, etc.
65	
66	    ``block_names`` preserves the *scheduling group* (which may contain more
67	    than one block when ``nblocks > 1``).  Pre-processing algorithms that
68	    only support single-block operation (e.g. AWQ Phase-1) must check
69	    ``len(block_names) == 1`` in ``prepare_block_group`` and raise
70	    ``ValueError`` with a user-readable message.
71	    """
72	
73	    model: "torch.nn.Module"
74	    block_names: list[str]  # scheduling group; len > 1 when nblocks > 1
75	    block_name: str  # = block_names[0] for single-block; descriptive label for multi
76	    block_index: int  # 0-based index within the current all_blocks group
77	    bs: int = 1
78	    is_mllm: bool = False  # fail-fast gate for algorithms that don't support MLLM
79	    is_diffusion: bool = False  # fail-fast gate for algorithms that don't support diffusion
80	    pbar: Any = None
81	    block_cnt: int = 0  # total number of blocks being quantized in this run

84	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	# AlgorithmComposer
86	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	class AlgorithmComposer:
88	    """An ordered composition of pre-processors + one block quantizer, built from
89	    a list of algorithm config objects and an optional compressor.
90	
91	    The ``preprocessors`` list is order-sensitive: algorithms are applied in
92	    the listed order (e.g. ``[Rotation, AWQ]``).  There must be **exactly one**
93	    ``block_quantizer`` (the terminal weight-compression step).
94	
95	    Usage::
96	
97	        composer = AlgorithmComposer(configs, compressor=self)
98	    """
99	
100	    def __init__(self, configs: list, orchestrator: "BaseOrchestrator" = None) -> None:
101	        """Build the pipeline from a list of algorithm config instances.
102	
103	        Resolution rules:
104	
105	        1. If no ``QuantizationConfig`` with a ``BaseQuantizer`` is found in
106	           *configs*, a default :class:`RTNConfig` is appended automatically.
107	        2. ``BasePreprocessor`` instances go into ``preprocessors`` (in order).
108	        3. Exactly one ``BaseQuantizer`` becomes ``block_quantizer``.
109	        4. Multiple block-quantization configs raise ``ValueError``.
110	        5. If *compressor* is provided, every member is bound to it and
111	           ``block_forward`` / quantization metadata are extracted from it.
112	
113	        Args:
114	            configs:    List of algorithm config objects (``QuantizationConfig``
115	                        subclasses such as :class:`RTNConfig`, :class:`SignRoundConfig`,
116	                        :class:`AWQConfig`, …).
117	            compressor: The :class:`~auto_round.compressors.base.BaseCompressor`
118	                        instance driving this pipeline.  When supplied, members are
119	                        bound to it and ``block_forward`` is taken from it.
120	        """
121	        from auto_round.algorithms.quantization.base import BaseQuantizer
122	        from auto_round.algorithms.quantization.config import QuantizationConfig
123	        from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.base import BasePreprocessor
124	
125	        configs = list(configs)
126	
127	        _, block_quantizer_configs = split_quantization_configs(configs)
128	        if not block_quantizer_configs:
129	            from auto_round.algorithms.quantization.rtn.config import RTNConfig
130	
131	            configs = configs + [RTNConfig()]
132	
133	        configs = resolve_shared_config_values(configs)
134	
135	        preprocessors: list = []
136	        block_quantizers: list = []
137	
138	        for cfg in configs:
139	            if not isinstance(cfg, QuantizationConfig):
140	                continue
141	            from auto_round.algorithms.registry import normalize_algorithm_config
142	
143	            cfg = normalize_algorithm_config(cfg)
144	            alg_cls = get_algorithm_class(cfg)
145	            if alg_cls is None:
146	                raise ValueError(f"Unknown algorithm config type {type(cfg).__name__!r}.")
147	            q = alg_cls(cfg)
148	            if orchestrator is not None:
149	                q.bind(orchestrator)
150	            if isinstance(q, BasePreprocessor):
151	                preprocessors.append(q)
152	            elif isinstance(q, BaseQuantizer):
153	                block_quantizers.append(q)
154	            else:
155	                raise TypeError(
156	                    f"Algorithm class {type(q).__name__} must inherit either " "BasePreprocessor or BaseQuantizer."
157	                )
158	
159	        if len(block_quantizers) > 1:
160	            raise ValueError(
161	                f"AlgorithmComposer allows exactly one block-quantization config, "
162	                f"but got {len(block_quantizers)}: "
163	                f"{[type(q).__name__ for q in block_quantizers]}. "
164	                "Ensure only one of RTNConfig / SignRoundConfig / etc. is in the pipeline."
165	            )
166	        if len(block_quantizers) == 0:
167	            raise ValueError("No block quantizer found in configs.")
168	
169	        seen = set()
170	        for pre in preprocessors:
171	            name = type(pre).__name__
172	            if name in seen:
173	                raise ValueError(
174	                    f"Duplicate preprocessor {name} in AlgorithmComposer. "
175	                    "Repeated instances of the same preprocessor are not supported yet."
176	                )
177	            seen.add(name)
178	
179	        self.preprocessors = preprocessors
180	
181	        # TODO wenhuach support multi quantizers
182	        can_compile_block_forward = False
183	        self.block_quantizer = block_quantizers[0]
184	        if orchestrator is not None:
185	            user_torch_compile = bool(
186	                getattr(getattr(orchestrator, "compress_context", None), "enable_torch_compile", False)
187	            )
188	            rotation_configs = getattr(orchestrator, "rotation_configs", ())
189	            blockers = []
190	            if not self.block_quantizer.can_compile_block_forward():
191	                blockers.append(type(self.block_quantizer).__name__)
192	            for component in [*self.preprocessors, *rotation_configs]:
193	                if not getattr(component, "can_compile_block_forward", lambda: True)():
194	                    blockers.append(type(component).__name__)
195	            can_compile_block_forward = user_torch_compile and not blockers
196	            if user_torch_compile and blockers:
197	                logger.info(
198	                    "Block-forward torch.compile is disabled because %s is incompatible.",
199	                    ", ".join(blockers),
200	                )
201	
202	            if _has_nvfp4_layer(orchestrator):
203	                can_compile_block_forward = False
204	                logger.info("Block-forward torch.compile is disabled because at least one quantized layer uses NVFP4.")
205	
206	            # Bind compressor-level infrastructure (set before _build_quantizer is called).
207	            self.block_forward = (
208	                BlockForwardRunner.from_orchestrator(orchestrator, enable_torch_compile=can_compile_block_forward)
209	                if orchestrator is not None
210	                else None
211	            )
212	            # A little tricky
213	            if self.block_quantizer is not None:
214	                self.block_quantizer.bind_block_forward_runner(self.block_forward)
215	        self.scheme = getattr(orchestrator, "scheme_context", None)

217	    # ── Internal hook helpers (act_max calibration) ───────────────────────────
218	
219	    def _register_act_max_hooks(self, block: "torch.nn.Module") -> list:
220	        """Register per-module act_max tracking hooks for static activation quantization.
221	
222	        Returns a list of hook handles that the caller must remove when done.
223	        """
224	        from auto_round.compressors.utils import is_nv_fp
225	        from auto_round.data_type.utils import reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size
226	
227	        is_act_nv_fp = getattr(self.block_quantizer.config, "is_act_nv_fp", False)
228	
229	        def collect_act_max(module, input, output):
230	            input = input[0] if isinstance(input, (tuple, list)) else input
231	            if input.numel() == 0:
232	                return
233	            module_act_data_type = getattr(module, "act_data_type", None) or getattr(module, "data_type", None)
234	            is_module_act_nv_fp = is_nv_fp(module_act_data_type) if module_act_data_type else is_act_nv_fp
235	            input, _, _ = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(input, module.act_group_size)
236	            act_max = torch.max(torch.abs(input), dim=-1).values
237	            if not hasattr(module, "act_max") or module.act_max.numel() == 0:
238	                module.act_max = act_max
239	                if is_module_act_nv_fp:
240	                    max_val = act_max.max()
241	                    module.act_max = max_val.unsqueeze(0) if max_val.dim() == 0 else max_val
242	                return
243	            act_max = act_max.to(module.act_max.device)
244	            if is_module_act_nv_fp:
245	                max_val = torch.max(act_max.max(), module.act_max.max())
246	                module.act_max = max_val.unsqueeze(0) if max_val.dim() == 0 else max_val
247	            else:
248	                module.act_max = torch.max(act_max, module.act_max)
249	
250	        def should_collect(name, module):
251	            from auto_round.compressors.utils import check_need_act_calibration
252	            from auto_round.utils import SUPPORTED_LAYER_TYPES, check_to_quantized
253	
254	            if isinstance(module, tuple(SUPPORTED_LAYER_TYPES)):
255	                return (
256	                    hasattr(module, "act_dynamic")
257	                    and check_need_act_calibration(module.act_dynamic, module.act_data_type, module.act_bits)
258	                    and check_to_quantized(module)
259	                )
260	            if hasattr(module, "bits"):
261	                act_dynamic = getattr(module, "act_dynamic", True)
262	                act_data_type = getattr(module, "act_data_type", None)
263	                act_bits = getattr(module, "act_bits", 16)
264	                return (
265	                    module.bits <= 8
266	                    and check_need_act_calibration(act_dynamic, act_data_type, act_bits)
267	                    and check_to_quantized(module)
268	                )
269	            return False
270	
271	        handles = []
272	        if should_collect("", block):
273	            handles.append(block.register_forward_hook(collect_act_max))
274	            return handles
275	        for name, module in block.named_modules():
276	            if name and should_collect(name, module):
277	                handles.append(module.register_forward_hook(collect_act_max))
278	        return handles
279	
280	    def _get_fp_act_hooks(self, block: "torch.nn.Module") -> list:
281	        """Register FP-input act_max + quantizer forward hooks."""
282	        if not self.need_quanted_input():
283	            # If having q_input, act_max will be collected in q_input forward hook,
284	            # no need to collect in fp_input forward hook
285	            handles = self._register_act_max_hooks(block)
286	        else:
287	            handles = []
288	        handles.extend(self.block_quantizer.register_fp_input_forward_hooks(block))
289	        return handles
290	
291	    def _get_q_act_hooks(self, block: "torch.nn.Module") -> list:
292	        """Register Q-input act_max + quantizer forward hooks."""
293	        handles = self._register_act_max_hooks(block)
294	        handles.extend(self.block_quantizer.register_qinput_forward_hooks(block))
295	        return handles

297	    def _attach_act_max_for_outside_layer(self, layer: "torch.nn.Module", fp_inputs, q_inputs) -> None:
298	        """Compute and attach act_max for an outside-block layer from cached inputs.
299	
300	        Mirrors the hook-based act_max collection done for in-block layers, but
301	        iterates over already-cached tensors directly instead of running a forward pass.
302	
303	        Args:
304	            layer: The layer module to attach act_max to.
305	            fp_inputs: List of FP input tensors collected during calibration.
306	            q_inputs: Optional list of quantized input tensors; used instead of
307	                ``fp_inputs`` when provided.
308	        """
309	        from auto_round.compressors.utils import is_nv_fp
310	        from auto_round.data_type.utils import reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size
311	
312	        target_input = q_inputs or fp_inputs
313	        act_group_size = getattr(layer, "act_group_size")
314	        if act_group_size is None:
315	            act_group_size = layer.group_size
316	        act_data_type = getattr(layer, "act_data_type")
317	        if act_data_type is None:
318	            act_data_type = layer.data_type
319	        is_act_nv_fp_flag = is_nv_fp(act_data_type) if act_data_type else False
320	
321	        for inp in target_input:
322	            if isinstance(inp, (tuple, list)):
323	                inp = inp[0]
324	            if inp.numel() == 0:
325	                continue
326	            inp, _, _ = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(inp, act_group_size)
327	            act_max = torch.max(torch.abs(inp), dim=-1).values
328	
329	            if not hasattr(layer, "act_max") or layer.act_max.numel() == 0:
330	                layer.act_max = act_max
331	                if is_act_nv_fp_flag:
332	                    max_val = act_max.max()
333	                    layer.act_max = max_val.unsqueeze(0) if max_val.dim() == 0 else max_val
334	                continue
335	
336	            act_max = act_max.to(layer.act_max.device)
337	            if is_act_nv_fp_flag:
338	                max_val = torch.max(act_max.max(), layer.act_max.max())
339	                layer.act_max = max_val.unsqueeze(0) if max_val.dim() == 0 else max_val
340	            else:
341	                layer.act_max = torch.max(act_max, layer.act_max)
342	
343	    def need_quanted_input(self):
344	        for preprocessor in self.preprocessors:
345	            if getattr(preprocessor, "enable_quanted_input", False):
346	                return True
347	        if getattr(self.block_quantizer, "enable_quanted_input", False):
348	            return True
349	        return False

352	        return self.block_quantizer.quantize_embedding_layer()

354	    # ── Per-block pipeline orchestration ─────────────────────────────────────
355	
356	    def compress_block(
357	        self,
358	        block,
359	        fp_inputs,
360	        input_others,
361	        block_ctx: BlockContext,
362	        q_inputs=None,
363	        input_ids=None,
364	        **kwargs,
365	    ) -> tuple:
366	        """Run the full per-block algorithm pipeline: calibration → quantization → collection.
367	
368	        Orchestrates preprocessors, quantizer calibration, and block quantization in
369	        the canonical order.  Infrastructure concerns (device management, memory cleanup,
370	        q_input variable reassignment) remain the caller's responsibility.
371	
372	        The interface mirrors :meth:`~auto_round.algorithms.quantization.base.BaseQuantizer.quantize_block`
373	        but covers the entire multi-step pipeline including preprocessor calibration and
374	        output collection.
375	
376	        Args:
377	            block: The transformer block to process.
378	            input_ids: Full-precision (FP) cached inputs.
379	            input_others: Auxiliary kwargs (attention_mask, position_ids, …).
380	            ctx: Per-block lifecycle context (:class:`BlockContext`).
381	            q_inputs: Quantized-input tensors from the previous block, or ``None``.
382	            valid_token_mask: Optional mask for per-token loss weighting.
383	
384	        Returns:
385	            ``(new_q_input, reference_output)``:
386	
387	            - *new_q_input*: block output after quantization (``None`` when
388	              ``enable_quanted_input`` is ``False``).
389	            - *reference_output*: FP reference output collected before optimization.
390	        """
391	        block_forward_fn = self.block_forward
392	
393	        # ── Step 1: Preprocessor calibration (e.g. AWQ activation stats) ──────
394	        with torch.no_grad():
395	            pre_hooks = []
396	            for pre in self.preprocessors:
397	                pre_hooks.extend(pre.register_fp_input_forward_hooks(block))
398	            if pre_hooks:
399	                block_forward_fn(block, fp_inputs, input_others)
400	            for h in pre_hooks:
401	                h.remove()
402	
403	            pre_q_hooks = []
404	            for pre in self.preprocessors:
405	                if hasattr(pre, "register_qinput_forward_hooks"):
406	                    pre_q_hooks.extend(pre.register_qinput_forward_hooks(block))
407	            if pre_q_hooks:
408	                block_forward_fn(block, q_inputs if q_inputs is not None else fp_inputs, input_others)
409	            for h in pre_q_hooks:
410	                h.remove()
411	
412	        # ── Step 2: pre_quantize_block (stats consolidation + weight transforms) ──
413	        for pre in self.preprocessors:
414	            pre.pre_quantize_block(block_ctx)
415	
416	        reference_output = None
417	        reference_next_input = None
418	        # ── Step 3: Quantizer calibration (act_max, imatrix, etc.) ─────────────
419	        if fp_inputs is not None:
420	            with torch.no_grad():
421	                quant_hooks = self._get_fp_act_hooks(block)
422	                reference_output = block_forward_fn(block, fp_inputs, input_others)
423	                reference_next_input = getattr(block_forward_fn, "last_output_dict", None) or reference_output
424	                for h in quant_hooks:
425	                    h.remove()
426	
427	                if self.block_quantizer.enable_quanted_input:
428	                    q_hooks = self._get_q_act_hooks(block)
429	                    if q_hooks:
430	                        block_forward_fn(block, q_inputs if q_inputs is not None else fp_inputs, input_others)
431	                        for h in q_hooks:
432	                            h.remove()
433	
434	            # ── Step 3.5: MoE scale alignment + global scale update ─────────────────
435	            # Must run after calibration hooks (act_max collected) and before quantize_block.
436	            act_dynamic = self.scheme.act_dynamic if (self.scheme and self.scheme.act_dynamic is not None) else True
437	            data_type = self.scheme.data_type if self.scheme else "int"
438	            group_size = self.scheme.group_size if self.scheme else -1
439	            act_data_type = self.scheme.act_data_type if self.scheme else data_type
440	            if act_data_type is not None or not act_dynamic:
441	                from auto_round.compressors.utils import is_nv_fp
442	                from auto_round.data_type.utils import update_block_global_scale_if_needed
443	                from auto_round.utils import set_amax_for_all_moe_layers
444	
445	                if is_nv_fp(act_data_type) or not act_dynamic:
446	                    set_amax_for_all_moe_layers(block, attr_name="act_max")
447	                update_block_global_scale_if_needed(block, data_type, group_size)
448	
449	        if q_inputs is not None and fp_inputs is not q_inputs:
450	            clear_memory(fp_inputs)
451	        else:
452	            clear_memory()
453	        # ── Step 4: quantize_block ──────────────────────────────────────────────
454	        # When quantized input is available from the previous block, use it;
455	        # otherwise fall back to the FP input.
456	        effective_input = q_inputs if q_inputs is not None else fp_inputs
457	        self.block_quantizer.quantize_block(
458	            block,
459	            effective_input,
460	            input_others,
461	            reference_output,
462	            q_inputs,
463	            block_ctx,
464	            input_ids=input_ids,
465	        )
466	
467	        # ── Step 5: post_quantize_block ─────────────────────────────────────────
468	        for pre in self.preprocessors:
469	            pre.post_quantize_block(block_ctx)
470	
471	        # ── Step 6: Collect quantized-block outputs for the next block ──────────
472	        if self.block_quantizer.enable_quanted_input:
473	            with torch.no_grad():
474	                new_q_input = block_forward_fn(block, effective_input, input_others)
475	                new_q_input = getattr(block_forward_fn, "last_output_dict", None) or new_q_input
476	        else:
477	            new_q_input = None
478	
479	        return new_q_input, reference_next_input
480	
481	    def compress_layer_outside_block(
482	        self,
483	        layer: "torch.nn.Module",
484	        fp_inputs=None,
485	        q_inputs=None,
486	        disable_opt_rtn=None,  # TODO wenhuach rename this to search_init_scale
487	        input_ids=None,
488	    ) -> None:
489	        """Quantize a single layer that lives outside transformer blocks.
490	
491	        Mirrors :meth:`compress_block` for the outside-block case: attaches
492	        act_max calibration when static activation quantization is required,
493	        then delegates to the block quantizer.
494	
495	        Args:
496	            layer: The layer module to quantize. Must have a ``global_name``
497	                attribute.
498	            fp_inputs: Per-sample FP activations for calibration, or ``None``
499	                to fall back to zero-shot RTN.
500	            q_inputs: Optional quantized activations from a previous stage.
501	            valid_token_mask: Per-sample token masks for loss weighting.
502	            disable_opt_rtn: Override optimized-RTN; ``None`` defers to quantizer config.
503	        """
504	        # Attach act_max for static activation quantization when inputs are available.
505	        if fp_inputs is not None:
506	            from auto_round.compressors.utils import is_nv_fp
507	
508	            act_data_type = getattr(layer, "act_data_type")
509	            if act_data_type is None:
510	                act_data_type = "fp"
511	            act_dynamic = getattr(layer, "act_dynamic", True)
512	            if is_nv_fp(act_data_type) or not act_dynamic:
513	                self._attach_act_max_for_outside_layer(layer, fp_inputs, q_inputs)
514	
515	        # Infrastructure: move layer to the tuning device before handing off to the quantizer.
516	        device = getattr(layer, "tuning_device", device_manager.device)  # TODO this should be handled by compressor
517	        layer = layer.to(device)
518	
519	        return self.block_quantizer.quantize_layer_outside_block(
520	            layer,
521	            fp_inputs=fp_inputs,
522	            q_inputs=q_inputs,
523	            disable_opt_rtn=disable_opt_rtn,
524	            input_ids=input_ids,
525	        )

528	
529	    def members(self) -> list:
530	        """Return all algorithm members: preprocessors followed by the block quantizer."""
531	        return list(self.preprocessors) + [self.block_quantizer]
532	
533	    def dispatch_block(self, block: "torch.nn.Module", input_ids, input_others: dict):
534	        """Dispatch block to device(s) via the pipeline's algorithms.
535	
536	        Iterates all members; if exactly one overrides the default dispatch_block,
537	        it is called. If multiple override, warns and uses the first one only.
538	        If none override, uses the block_quantizer's default (simple .to(device)).
539	        """
540	        from auto_round.algorithms.quantization.base import BaseQuantizer
541	
542	        overriders = []
543	        for member in self.members():
544	            if not hasattr(member, "dispatch_block"):
545	                continue
546	            # Check if the member overrides the base default
547	            if type(member).dispatch_block is not BaseQuantizer.dispatch_block:
548	                overriders.append(member)
549	
550	        if len(overriders) > 1:
551	            names = [type(m).__name__ for m in overriders]
552	            logger.warning(
553	                f"Multiple pipeline members override dispatch_block: {names}. "
554	                f"Only {names[0]} will be used; others are ignored."
555	            )
556	
557	        if overriders:
558	            return overriders[0].dispatch_block(block, input_ids, input_others)
559	        return self.block_quantizer.dispatch_block(block, input_ids, input_others)
560	
561	    def prepare_run(self, composer: "AlgorithmComposer" = None):
562	        for alg in self.members():
563	            alg.prepare_run(composer=self)
564	
565	    def finalize_run(self):
566	        for alg in self.members():
567	            alg.finalize_run()

4	"""Algorithm discovery, registration, listing, and config building for the CLI.
5	
6	To add a new algorithm:
7	1. Write a class that extends AlgorithmHandler and set name/aliases/summary.
8	2. Implement register(group) to declare argparse flags.
9	3. Implement build(args, common_kwargs) to return a config object.
10	
11	No manual registry update needed — subclasses are auto-registered on definition.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import argparse
17	import copy
18	from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
19	from typing import Any, ClassVar
20	
21	from auto_round.algorithms.registry import (
22	    get_algorithm_entry,
23	    iter_algorithm_entries,
24	    register_algorithm,
25	    resolve_algorithm_alias,
26	    resolve_algorithm_names,
27	)
28	
29	# ============================================================================
30	# Base class + registry
31	# ============================================================================
32	
33	
34	class AlgorithmHandler(ABC):
35	    """Bundles everything the CLI needs to know about one algorithm.
36	
37	    Concrete subclasses are auto-registered in the class-level registry
38	    the moment their class body is processed.
39	    """
40	
41	    name: str  # canonical name used in --algorithm
42	    aliases: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # all accepted names, including canonical
43	    summary: str = ""  # one-liner shown by `auto_round list alg`
44	    config_factory: ClassVar[type | None] = None
45	
46	    def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs) -> None:
47	        super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
48	        # A class that overrides both register and build is considered a concrete
49	        # algorithm implementation and must also declare a `name` class attribute.
50	        if "register" in cls.__dict__ and "build" in cls.__dict__:
51	            if "name" not in cls.__dict__:
52	                raise TypeError(f"{cls.__name__} must define a 'name' class attribute " f"(e.g. name = 'my_algo').")
53	            register_algorithm(
54	                cls.name,
55	                aliases=cls.aliases,
56	                config_factory=cls.config_factory,
57	                cli_handler=cls,
58	                summary=cls.summary,
59	            )
60	
61	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
62	    # Abstract interface — implement in each subclass
63	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
64	
65	    @abstractmethod
66	    def register(self, group) -> None:
67	        """Add argparse arguments to *group*."""
68	
69	    @abstractmethod
70	    def build(self, args, common_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
71	        """Build and return an algorithm config from parsed *args*."""
72	
73	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
74	    # Registry operations — called on the class, not on instances
75	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
76	
77	    @classmethod
78	    def get(cls, name: str) -> AlgorithmHandler:
79	        """Return the handler for a canonical algorithm name. Raises KeyError if unknown."""
80	        entry = get_algorithm_entry(name)
81	        if entry.cli_handler is None:
82	            raise KeyError(f"No handler registered for algorithm '{name}'.")
83	        return entry.cli_handler()
84	
85	    @classmethod
86	    def resolve_alias(cls, user_name: str) -> str | None:
87	        """Resolve a user-supplied algorithm name or alias to the canonical name.
88	
89	        Returns None instead of raising so callers can silently skip unknowns.
90	        """
91	        return resolve_algorithm_alias(user_name)
92	
93	    @classmethod
94	    def add_groups(cls, parser) -> None:
95	        """Add an argparse argument group for every registered algorithm."""
96	        for entry in iter_algorithm_entries():
97	            if entry.cli_handler is None:
98	                continue
99	            handler = entry.cli_handler()
100	            group = parser.add_argument_group(f"Algorithm: {handler.name}")
101	            handler.register(group)
102	
103	    @classmethod
104	    def build_configs(cls, args, common_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> list:
105	        """Build the ordered algorithm config list from parsed CLI args."""
106	        raw = getattr(args, "algorithm", None) or ""
107	        names = [n.strip().lower() for n in raw.split(",") if n.strip()]
108	
109	        # Infer hadamard when --rotation_type is given
110	        if getattr(args, "rotation_hadamard_type", None) and "hadamard" not in names:
111	            names.append("hadamard")
112	
113	        # Resolve aliases, drop unknowns, deduplicate preserving order.
114	        # Python API strings use this same resolver so their composition
115	        # semantics cannot drift apart again.
116	        canonical = resolve_algorithm_names(names, ignore_unknown=True)
117	        seen = set(canonical)
118	
119	        # Default terminal quantizer if none was specified. AWQ is a
120	        # calibration preprocessor; AWQ-only pipelines intentionally default to
121	        # RTN so RTN CLI flags such as --disable_opt_rtn are applied before the
122	        # lower-level composer has to append a fallback quantizer.
123	        if not ({"rtn", "auto_round"} & seen):
124	            default_quantizer = "rtn" if "awq" in seen or getattr(args, "iters", 0) == 0 else "auto_round"
125	            canonical.append(default_quantizer)
126	
127	        # Keep the legacy API rule even when the user explicitly spells out
128	        # ``--algorithm auto_round``: zero iterations select RTN.
129	        if getattr(args, "iters", None) == 0:
130	            canonical = ["rtn" if name == "auto_round" else name for name in canonical]
131	
132	        explicit_opt_rtn = getattr(args, "disable_opt_rtn", None) is not None
133	        awq_config = cls.get("awq").build(args, common_kwargs) if "awq" in canonical else None
134	        awq_disable_opt_rtn = getattr(awq_config, "disable_opt_rtn", None)
135	
136	        configs = []
137	        for name in canonical:
138	            if name == "awq":
139	                configs.append(awq_config)
140	                continue
141	            build_args = args
142	            if name == "rtn" and not explicit_opt_rtn and awq_disable_opt_rtn is not None:
143	                build_args = copy.copy(args)
144	                setattr(build_args, "disable_opt_rtn", awq_disable_opt_rtn)
145	            configs.append(cls.get(name).build(build_args, common_kwargs))
146	        return configs

150	        """Render the short `list alg` output."""
151	        lines = []
152	        for entry in iter_algorithm_entries():
153	            if entry.cli_handler is None:
154	                continue
155	            handler = entry.cli_handler()
156	            other = [a for a in handler.aliases if a != handler.name]
157	            alias_str = f" (aliases: {', '.join(other)})" if other else ""
158	            lines.append(f"- {handler.name}{alias_str}: {handler.summary}")

166	            supported = [entry.name for entry in iter_algorithm_entries() if entry.cli_handler is not None]
167	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown algorithm '{name}'. " f"Supported: {', '.join(supported)}.")
168	        handler = cls.get(canon)
169	        lines = [f"{handler.name}: {handler.summary}"]
170	        other = [a for a in handler.aliases if a != handler.name]
171	        if other:

173	        temp = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
174	        group = temp.add_argument_group(f"Flags for {handler.name}")
175	        handler.register(group)
176	        for action in group._group_actions:
177	            flags = ", ".join(action.option_strings)
178	            default = f" (default: {action.default})" if action.default is not None else ""
179	            lines.append(f"  {flags}: {action.help or ''}{default}")

147	        per-layer values are computed later via ``compute_lr``/``compute_minmax_lr``.
148	        """
149	        # Track whether the values are auto-derived so per-layer bit widths can
150	        # be honored during optimization (see compute_lr/compute_minmax_lr).
151	        self.lr_is_auto = self.lr is None and self.iters > 0
152	        self.minmax_lr_is_auto = self.minmax_lr is None
153	        if self.lr_is_auto:

139	    def _init_tuning_params_and_quant_func(self):
140	        """Initializes tuning parameters and quantization functions.
141	
142	        This method sets up required parameters and functions for weight quantization,
143	        activation quantization, and bias/normalization.
144	        """
145	        self.params = {}
146	        p_dtype = torch.float32  ##parameter dtype
147	
148	        orig_layer = self.orig_layer
149	        orig_weight = getattr(orig_layer, "get_weight", lambda: orig_layer.weight)()
150	        if type(self.orig_layer) == transformers.pytorch_utils.Conv1D:
151	            orig_weight = orig_weight.t()
152	        weight_reshape, _, _ = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(orig_weight.data, orig_layer.group_size)
153	
154	        if self.enable_round_tuning:
155	            self.weight_min = (
156	                torch.clamp(weight_reshape.amin(dim=(-2, -1)), max=0)
157	                if isinstance(orig_layer.group_size, tuple)
158	                else torch.clamp(weight_reshape.min(1)[0], max=0)
159	            )
160	            self.weight_max = (
161	                torch.clamp(weight_reshape.amax(dim=(-2, -1)), min=0)
162	                if isinstance(orig_layer.group_size, tuple)
163	                else torch.clamp(weight_reshape.max(1)[0], min=0)
164	            )
165	        else:
166	            self.weight_min = None
167	            self.weight_max = None
168	        # AWQ clip-as-init: cap the tunable weight range to the per-group clip
169	        # range searched by AWQ (``apply_clip`` with ``clip_as_init=True``).
170	        # This initializes the range used by quant_tensor_sym/asym, leaving
171	        # min_scale/max_scale to tune a coefficient on top. Only the standard
172	        # (non-tuple) group layout maps onto weight_min/weight_max here.
173	        awq_clip_min = getattr(orig_layer, "awq_clip_min", None)
174	        awq_clip_max = getattr(orig_layer, "awq_clip_max", None)
175	        if awq_clip_max is not None and self.weight_min is not None and not isinstance(orig_layer.group_size, tuple):
176	            clip_max_flat = awq_clip_max.reshape(-1).to(self.weight_max.device, self.weight_max.dtype)
177	            if awq_clip_min is None:
178	                clip_min_flat = -clip_max_flat
179	            else:
180	                clip_min_flat = awq_clip_min.reshape(-1).to(self.weight_min.device, self.weight_min.dtype)
181	            if clip_max_flat.numel() == self.weight_max.numel() and clip_min_flat.numel() == self.weight_min.numel():
182	                self.weight_max = torch.minimum(self.weight_max, clip_max_flat)
183	                self.weight_min = torch.maximum(self.weight_min, clip_min_flat)
184	        self._init_params(
185	            "value", p_dtype, weight_reshape.shape, 0, self.enable_round_tuning and self.orig_layer.bits < 16
186	        )
187	        # Min-max scale initialization
188	        shape = get_scale_shape(orig_weight, orig_layer.group_size)
189	        self._init_params("min_scale", p_dtype, shape, 1.0, (self.enable_minmax_tuning and self.orig_layer.bits < 16))
190	        self._init_params("max_scale", p_dtype, shape, 1.0, (self.enable_minmax_tuning and self.orig_layer.bits < 16))
191	
192	        self.weight_quant_func, self.data_type = get_quant_func(
193	            orig_layer.data_type,
194	            orig_layer.bits,
195	            orig_layer.sym,
196	            self.disable_opt_rtn,
197	            orig_layer.group_size,
198	            iters=orig_layer.iters,
199	        )
200	        if self.enable_torch_compile:
201	            self.weight_quant_func = compile_func(self.weight_quant_func, self.device)
202	
203	        if self.enable_act_quant:
204	            self.act_quant_func, self.act_data_type = get_quant_func(
205	                orig_layer.act_data_type,
206	                orig_layer.act_bits,
207	                orig_layer.act_sym,
208	                disable_opt_rtn=True,
209	                iters=orig_layer.iters,
210	            )
211	            if self.enable_torch_compile:
212	                self.act_quant_func = compile_func(self.act_quant_func, self.device)
213	            self._init_params(
214	                "act_max_scale", p_dtype, (1), 1.0, envs.AR_ENABLE_ACT_MINMAX_TUNING or (not orig_layer.act_dynamic)
215	            )
216	            self._init_params("act_min_scale", p_dtype, (1), 1.0, envs.AR_ENABLE_ACT_MINMAX_TUNING)
217	
218	        # Bias tuning
219	        if self.enable_norm_bias_tuning:
220	            self._init_params("bias_v", p_dtype, self.orig_layer.bias.shape, 0, True)
221	            from auto_round.data_type.int import quant_tensor_asym_wo_round

223	            self.bias_quant_func = quant_tensor_asym_wo_round

226	    def _init_params(self, name, dtype, shape, value, tunable):
227	        """Initializes a parameter for tuning or uses a constant if tuning is disabled.
228	
229	        Args:
230	            name (str): Name of the parameter.
231	            dtype (torch.dtype): Data type of the parameter.
232	            shape (tuple): Shape of the parameter.

50	def _dq_asym_qdq(tensor, scale, wmin, bits, group_size, v=0):
51	    """Pure asym double-quant qdq math given precomputed scale/wmin (compilable)."""
52	    tensor, orig_shape, pad_len = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(tensor, group_size)
53	    orig_dtype = tensor.dtype
54	    tensor = tensor.to(torch.float32)
55	    maxq = int(2.0**bits) - 1
56	    inverse_scale = get_reciprocal(scale)
57	    int_w = torch.clamp(round_ste((tensor + wmin) * inverse_scale + v), 0, maxq)
58	    qdq = (scale * int_w - wmin).to(orig_dtype)
59	    qdq = revert_tensor_by_pad(qdq, orig_shape=orig_shape, pad_len=pad_len)
60	    return qdq

63	def _dq_sym_qdq(tensor, scale, bits, v=0):
64	    """Pure sym double-quant qdq math given precomputed scale (compilable)."""
65	    from auto_round.export.export_to_gguf.config import GGML_QUANT_SIZES, QK_K
66	
67	    group_size = 16
68	    super_group_size = 16
69	    maxq = int(2.0 ** (bits - 1))
70	    tensor, orig_shape, pad_len = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(tensor, group_size)
71	    orig_dtype = tensor.dtype
72	    tensor = tensor.to(torch.float32)
73	    ggml_type = f"q{bits}_k"
74	    block_size, _ = GGML_QUANT_SIZES[ggml_type]
75	    n_blocks = tensor.nelement() // block_size
76	    tensor = tensor.reshape(n_blocks, super_group_size, QK_K // super_group_size)
77	    if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
78	        v_r, _, _ = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(v, group_size)
79	        v_r = v_r.reshape(n_blocks, super_group_size, QK_K // super_group_size)
80	    else:
81	        v_r = v
82	    zp = torch.full_like(scale, maxq)
83	    inverse_scale = get_reciprocal(scale)
84	    int_w = round_ste(tensor * inverse_scale + v_r).clip(-maxq, maxq - 1) + maxq
85	    qdq = (scale * (int_w - zp)).to(orig_dtype)
86	    qdq = revert_tensor_by_pad(qdq, orig_shape=orig_shape, pad_len=pad_len)
87	    return qdq

128	    def _prepare_init_scale_weight(self) -> torch.Tensor:
129	        """Return the group-reshaped weight that seeds the init-scale search.
130	
131	        Reproduces the layout the quant func sees at tuning time: the (optionally
132	        transposed) FP weight grouped to ``[-1, group_size]``. When AWQ ran in
133	        ``clip_as_init`` mode and stored a per-group clip range on the layer, the
134	        weight is clamped to that range first so the searched ``init_scale``
135	        already reflects the AWQ clip (``max_scale`` then tunes a coefficient on
136	        top of it).
137	        """
138	        layer = self.orig_layer
139	        weight = layer.get_weight() if hasattr(layer, "get_weight") else layer.weight
140	        if isinstance(layer, transformers.pytorch_utils.Conv1D):
141	            weight = weight.t()
142	        weight_reshape, _, _ = reshape_pad_tensor_by_group_size(weight.data, layer.group_size)
143	
144	        clip_min = getattr(layer, "awq_clip_min", None)
145	        clip_max = getattr(layer, "awq_clip_max", None)
146	        if clip_max is not None:
147	            clip_max = clip_max.reshape(-1, 1).to(weight_reshape.device, weight_reshape.dtype)
148	            clip_min = (
149	                -clip_max
150	                if clip_min is None
151	                else clip_min.reshape(-1, 1).to(weight_reshape.device, weight_reshape.dtype)
152	            )
153	            if clip_max.shape[0] == weight_reshape.shape[0] and clip_min.shape[0] == weight_reshape.shape[0]:
154	                weight_reshape = torch.clamp(weight_reshape, clip_min, clip_max)
155	            else:
156	                logger.warning_once(
157	                    "SignRoundV2: ignoring AWQ clip range with shapes %s/%s incompatible with "
158	                    "grouped weight shape %s."
159	                    % (tuple(clip_min.shape), tuple(clip_max.shape), tuple(weight_reshape.shape))
160	                )
161	        return weight_reshape

1	# Rotation Transform — Details (Research)
2	
3	> ⚠️ **Research feature.** Rotation transform is still in a research stage. Inference relies on forward hooks, which are currently only supported by the Hugging Face Transformers backend. As a result, inference may be slower compared to native (non-rotated) models.
4	
5	This document is the in-depth reference for AutoRound's rotation transforms. For a
6	concise getting-started guide, see the *Rotation* section in
7	[step_by_step.md](./step_by_step.md).
8	
9	Rotation redistributes outliers in weights and activations before quantization by
10	multiplying tensors with orthogonal (Hadamard) matrices. Because an orthogonal
11	rotation `R` satisfies `R @ Rᵀ = I`, a matched pair of rotations inserted around a
12	linear operation leaves the network's output unchanged (`x @ R @ Rᵀ @ Wᵀ = x @ Wᵀ`)
13	while making the intermediate distributions flatter and more quantization-friendly.
14	This is most useful for aggressive low-bit schemes such as MXFP4, NVFP4 and W4A4.
15	
16	AutoRound provides two independent rotation implementations:
17	
18	- **QuaRot / SpinQuant** — architecture-aware, full-model rotation applied at up to
19	  four positions (R1–R4). Selected via `rotation_config="quarot"`,
20	  `rotation_config="spinquant"`, or a `SpinQuantConfig` instance. **Recommended.**
21	- **Per-Linear Block Rotation** — an earlier, simpler implementation that applies a
22	  block-diagonal Hadamard uniformly to every `nn.Linear`. Selected via
23	  `rotation_config="default"` / a string Hadamard type, or a `RotationConfig`
24	  instance. Also exposed through the `--algorithm hadamard` CLI.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. QuaRot / SpinQuant
29	
30	QuaRot applies deterministic Hadamard rotations at up to four positions in the
31	transformer architecture. Unlike per-linear block rotation, it operates at the model
32	architecture level — rotating the residual stream, attention heads, and MLP
33	activations at specific positions for targeted outlier suppression.
34	
35	The pipeline (implemented in `auto_round/algorithms/transforms/spinquant/preprocessor.py`,
36	`SpinQuantPreprocessor`) runs the following stages:
37	
38	1. Fuse RMSNorm scale parameters into the following linear layers (`fuse_rmsnorm`).
39	2. Untie word embeddings if they are shared with the LM head (`untie_embeddings`).
40	3. Initialize rotation matrices R1–R4.
41	4. (Only if trainable) train the rotations and smooth values via KL/MSE loss.
42	5. Fuse the offline rotations (R2, and R1 when `online_r1_rotation=False`) into weights.
43	6. Register the online hooks (R1 when online, R3, R4) and clean up.
44	
45	### 1.1 Rotation positions
46	
47	| Position | Target | Dimension | Mode | Effect |
48	|----------|--------|-----------|------|--------|
49	| **R1** | Residual stream — inputs of `q/k/v_proj`, `gate/up_proj`; outputs of `o_proj`, `down_proj`, `embed_tokens`, `lm_head` | `hidden_size` (or `rotation_size`) | Online *or* Offline | Smooths weight outliers across all linear layers |
50	| **R2** | `v_proj` output / `o_proj` input (per attention head) | `head_dim` | Offline (fused) | Balances per-head value distributions |
51	| **R3** | Q/K after RoPE | `head_dim` | Online (RoPE monkeypatch) | Improves KV-cache quantization friendliness |
52	| **R4** | `down_proj` input (MLP activation) | `intermediate_size` (or `rotation_size`) | Online (hook) + weight fuse | Suppresses activation outliers in the FFN |
53	
54	- **Online**: applied at runtime via forward hooks / a RoPE monkeypatch. Weights are
55	  pre-rotated so the paired inverse rotation happens at runtime; there is a small
56	  inference cost.
57	- **Offline (fused)**: the rotation is absorbed into adjacent weight matrices, leaving
58	  no runtime overhead.
59	
60	R1 is applied online by default (`online_r1_rotation=True`): the target weights are
61	rotated and a `forward_pre_hook` is registered on the same modules. When
62	`online_r1_rotation=False`, R1 is instead fully fused into `embed_tokens`,
63	`q/k/v_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate/up/down_proj` and `lm_head`, cancelling out with no
64	runtime cost.
65	
66	### 1.2 `SpinQuantConfig` reference
67	
68	Defined in `auto_round/algorithms/transforms/spinquant/preprocessor.py`.
69	
70	| Field | Default | Description |
71	|-------|---------|-------------|
72	| `algorithm` | `"spinquant"` | Registry key used by `BaseRotation.from_config()` to dispatch. |
73	| `r1` | `True` | Enable R1 (hidden_size residual-stream rotation). |
74	| `r2` | `True` | Enable R2 (head_dim per-head rotation, offline). |
75	| `r3` | `False` | Enable R3 (online Q/K rotation after RoPE). |
76	| `r4` | `False` | Enable R4 (online MLP activation rotation). |
77	| `rotation_size` | `None` (auto) | Overrides the R1/R4 block size (R1 uses it instead of `hidden_size`, R4 instead of `intermediate_size`). R2 always uses `head_dim`; R3 has no custom size. Must be a positive power of 2. |
78	| `random_r1` / `random_r2` / `random_r3` / `random_r4` | `False` | Use random Hadamard (`H × diag(±1)`) instead of the deterministic matrix at that position. Only relevant in QuaRot mode. |
79	| `online_r1_rotation` | `True` | Apply R1 online via hook (`True`) or fuse it fully into weights (`False`). |
80	| `trainable_rotation` | `False` | Learn the rotation matrices via Cayley SGD (SpinQuant mode). **Research**, requires a dataloader. |
81	| `trainable_smooth` | `False` | Learn SmoothQuant-style `smooth_values` jointly via Adam. **Research**, requires a dataloader. |
82	| `iters` | `200` | Training iterations (trainable modes only). |
83	| `lr` | `1e-4` | SGDG (Cayley) learning rate for rotation matrices. |
84	| `smooth_lr` | `1e-3` | Adam learning rate for smooth values. |
85	| `batch_size` | `1` | Training batch size. |
86	| `loss_type` | `"kl_top"` | Training loss: `"kl_top"`, `"kl_full"`, or `"mse"`. |
87	| `kl_top_k` | `1000` | Top-k logits used by the `kl_top` loss. |
88	| `fuse_rmsnorm` | `True` | Fuse RMSNorm scales into following linear layers. |
89	| `untie_embeddings` | `True` | Untie shared embedding / LM-head weights before rotating. |
90	| `dtype` | `torch.float32` | Numerical dtype used for rotation math. |
91	| `device` | `None` (auto) | Defaults to `"cuda"` if available, else `"cpu"`. |
92	
93	### 1.3 String shortcuts
94	
95	| Value | Equivalent |
96	|-------|-----------|
97	| `"quarot"` | `SpinQuantConfig(trainable_rotation=False, trainable_smooth=False)` — deterministic Hadamard, no training, no calibration data. |
98	| `"spinquant"` | `SpinQuantConfig(trainable_rotation=True, trainable_smooth=True)` — **research**, requires a dataloader. |
99	
100	Both presets keep the default `r1=True, r2=True, r3=False, r4=False`. A dict with
101	`algorithm="spinquant"` is also parsed into a `SpinQuantConfig`.
102	
103	> ⚠️ **SpinQuant trainable rotation** (`trainable_rotation=True`) enables learnable
104	> rotation matrices optimized via Cayley SGD. This feature is a research feature and not
105	> fully validated on real models. Use `"quarot"` (fixed Hadamard) for production
106	> workloads.
107	
108	### 1.4 Usage
109	
110	```python
111	from auto_round import AutoRound
112	from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.spinquant import SpinQuantConfig
113	
114	model_name = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
115	
116	# QuaRot preset: R1+R2 deterministic Hadamard, no training
117	ar = AutoRound(model_name, scheme="MXFP4", rotation_config="quarot")
118	
119	# Choose how many positions to rotate:
120	ar = AutoRound(model_name, scheme="MXFP4", rotation_config=SpinQuantConfig(r1=True))  # R1 only
121	ar = AutoRound(model_name, scheme="MXFP4", rotation_config=SpinQuantConfig(r1=True, r2=True))  # R1+R2
122	ar = AutoRound(
123	    model_name, scheme="MXFP4", rotation_config=SpinQuantConfig(r1=True, r2=True, r3=True, r4=True)
124	)  # all four
125	
126	ar.quantize_and_save(output_dir="./Qwen3-0.6B-mxfp4-quarot", format="auto_round")
127	```
128	
129	### 1.5 Deterministic vs random Hadamard
130	
131	Rotation matrices are constructed in
132	`auto_round/algorithms/transforms/spinquant/rotation_utils.py`:
133	
134	- **Deterministic** (default): `deterministic_hadamard_matrix(size)` builds a Sylvester
135	  Hadamard matrix (`H → [[H, H], [H, −H]]`) normalized by `√size`. The size must be a
136	  power of 2. Because the matrix is fully determined by its size, nothing needs to be
137	  stored.
138	- **Random**: `random_hadamard_matrix(size)` computes `H @ diag(±1) / √N`. It offers
139	  slightly better outlier suppression but the sign matrix must be persisted.
140	
141	For non-power-of-2 dimensions, `get_hadamard_K(n)` factors `n = K · 2^m` and pulls a
142	known base Hadamard of size `K` (e.g. 12, 20, 28, 36, 40, 52, 60, 108, 140, 156, 172)
143	from `known_hadamard.py`, combining it with a Sylvester block.
144	
145	```python
146	# Random Hadamard at every enabled position
147	ar = AutoRound(
148	    model_name,
149	    scheme="MXFP4",
150	    rotation_config=SpinQuantConfig(
151	        r1=True,
152	        r2=True,
153	        r3=True,
154	        r4=True,
155	        random_r1=True,
156	        random_r2=True,
157	        random_r3=True,
158	        random_r4=True,
159	    ),
160	)
161	```
162	
163	### 1.6 Trainable rotation (SpinQuant mode)
164	
165	When `trainable_rotation=True` (and/or `trainable_smooth=True`), the rotations become
166	learnable and are optimized on calibration data:
167	
168	- `cayley_optimizer.py` provides `SGDG`, an orthogonality-preserving optimizer that
169	  keeps each rotation on the Stiefel manifold using a Cayley/QR retraction.
170	  `AdamAndSGDG` combines Adam (for `smooth_values`) with SGDG (for the `spinquant_R*`
171	  matrices).
172	- `training.py` runs a KL-/MSE-based distillation loop against a frozen clone of the
173	  original model (`create_dual_optimizer()`, `run_training_loop()`).
174	- `SpinQuantPreprocessor.preprocess()` **requires a dataloader** whenever either
175	  trainable flag is set.
176	
177	### 1.7 Save & load
178	
179	Quantized models with rotation are saved and loaded transparently. Serialization lives
180	in `auto_round/algorithms/transforms/spinquant/serialize.py`.
181	
182	```python
183	# Save (rotation matrices stored automatically when needed)
184	ar.quantize_and_save(output_dir="./my_model", format="auto_round")
185	
186	# Load (rotation hooks restored automatically)
187	from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
188	
189	model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("./my_model", device_map="auto")
190	```
191	
192	What is stored per position (metadata keys prefixed with `spinquant_r1` / `spinquant_r4`,
193	with a `*_type` code: `0` = deterministic, `1` = random, `2` = trained):
194	
195	- **Deterministic rotations**: only metadata (type + `rotation_size`) — the matrix is
196	  reconstructed on load.
197	- **Random rotations**: an `int8` (±1) matrix is stored (size ≈ `rotation_size²` bytes).
198	- **Trained rotations**: the full `float32` matrix is stored.
199	- **Online rotations**: rebuilt during model loading — `preregister_spinquant_buffers()`
200	  creates empty buffers before the `state_dict` load, and `rebuild_spinquant_online()`
201	  re-patches the QuantLinear forward (R1/R4) and re-applies the R3 RoPE monkeypatch.
202	  R3 is rebuilt purely from `config.json`, not from stored buffers.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## 2. Per-Linear Block Rotation
207	
208	> ⚠️ This is an earlier research implementation that applies block-diagonal
209	> Hadamard rotation **per linear layer** by patching every `nn.Linear` module in the
210	> model. For most use cases the QuaRot / SpinQuant approach above is preferred — it
211	> provides architecture-aware rotation at specific positions (R1–R4) with better
212	> accuracy and lower overhead.
213	
214	The per-linear block rotation iterates over all linear layers and applies a Hadamard of
215	a configurable `block_size` uniformly. It does not distinguish between residual stream,
216	attention and MLP layers, nor does it handle RoPE or attention-side rotation. It is
217	configured with `RotationConfig`
218	(`auto_round/algorithms/transforms/hadamard/config.py`), which is shared by three
219	backends:
220	
221	| `backend` | Behaviour |
222	|-----------|-----------|
223	| `"inplace"` | QuaRot-style residual-stream rotation; works for any dtype and can fuse the online Hadamard into weights (`fuse_online_to_weight=True`). |
224	| `"transform"` | Per-Linear weight + activation Hadamard with a fused Triton kernel; supports only MXFP4 / NVFP4 and cannot fuse online to weight. |
225	| `"auto"` (default) | Picks `inplace` when a fused online rotation is requested, `transform` for MX/NV-FP data types, `inplace` otherwise. |
226	
227	Application modes (`hadamard/apply.py`):
228	
229	- **Input mode**: registers a `forward_pre_hook` that rotates the input activation
230	  before each linear layer (online).
231	- **Weight mode**: fuses the Hadamard directly into the module weight (offline) and
232	  patches the calibration wrappers accordingly.
233	
234	### 2.1 `RotationConfig` reference
235	
236	| Field | Default | Description |
237	|-------|---------|-------------|
238	| `algorithm` | `"hadamard"` (frozen) | Registry key. |
239	| `backend` | `"auto"` | `"auto"`, `"inplace"`, or `"transform"`. |
240	| `block_size` | `None` (auto) | Grouped Hadamard block size. Auto-filled from the data type by `normalize_rotation_config()`: **32** for MXFP, **16** for NVFP. `None`/`-1` means full-dimension Hadamard. |
241	| `hadamard_type` | `"hadamard"` | One of `hadamard`, `random_hadamard`, `inplace_quarot_hadamard`, `inplace_hadamard`, `inplace_random`. Deterministic Hadamard uses Sylvester construction (`block_size` must be a power of 2); `random_hadamard` supports non-power-of-2 sizes from the known-matrix library. |
242	| `fuse_online_to_weight` | `None` | Fuse online Hadamard rotation into weights when supported (`inplace` backend only). |
243	| `allow_online_rotation` | `True` | Allow online activation rotation. |
244	
245	### 2.2 Usage
246	
247	```python
248	from auto_round import AutoRound
249	
250	model_name_or_path = "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"
251	
252	# rotation_config="default": block_size auto (32 for MXFP), hadamard_type="hadamard"
253	ar = AutoRound(model_name_or_path, scheme="MXFP4", rotation_config="default")
254	ar.quantize_and_save(output_dir="./Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-mxfp4-ht", format="auto_round")
255	```
256	
257	The per-linear rotation is also exposed on the CLI via `--algorithm hadamard`:
258	
259	```bash
260	auto-round --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --scheme MXFP4 \
261	  --algorithm hadamard --rotation_type hadamard --rotation_backend auto
262	```
263	
264	CLI flags: `--rotation_type {hadamard,random_hadamard,quarot_hadamard}`,
265	`--rotation_backend {auto,inplace,transform}`, `--rotation_block_size N`,
266	`--fuse_online_to_weight` / `--no-fuse_online_to_weight`,
267	`--allow_online_rotation` / `--no-allow_online_rotation`.
268	
269	---
270	
271	## 3. How `rotation_config` is dispatched
272	
273	`rotation_config` is accepted by `AutoRound` and normalized by the unified
274	`apply_rotation()` entry point in
275	`auto_round/algorithms/transforms/__init__.py`:
276	
277	- A `BaseRotationConfig` instance (`SpinQuantConfig` or `RotationConfig`) is used
278	  directly.
279	- The strings `"quarot"` / `"spinquant"` map to the `SpinQuantConfig` shortcuts above.
280	- A dict with `algorithm="spinquant"` becomes a `SpinQuantConfig`.
281	- Any other string (e.g. `"default"`, `"hadamard"`, `"random_hadamard"`) or dict maps to
282	  the per-linear `RotationConfig`.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 4. Example Results
287	
288	Enabling rotation consistently recovers accuracy lost to aggressive low-bit
289	quantization. The tables below compare three configurations for each model:
290	
291	- **BF16** — the unquantized baseline (reference, 100%).
292	- **MXFP4** — MXFP4 quantization without rotation.
293	- **MXFP4 + rotation** — MXFP4 quantization with the QuaRot-style rotation shown in
294	  the *Rotation* column.
295	
296	All numbers were measured with [lm-eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness)
297	on four tasks — **GSM8K**, **MMLU**, **PIQA** and **HellaSwag**. **Avg** is the mean
298	across the four tasks and **Ratio** is that average relative to the BF16 baseline.
299	Higher is better. Across all three model sizes (8B, 32B and 72B), rotation improves the
300	MXFP4 average and closes the gap to BF16.
301	
302	**Qwen3-8B** — rotation lifts MXFP4 from 93.77% to 95.73% of BF16 (+1.96 pts), with
303	the largest gains on the quantization-sensitive MMLU and PIQA tasks.
304	
305	| Model | Scheme | Rotation | GSM8K (strict, acc) | MMLU (acc) | PIQA (acc) | HellaSwag (acc) | Avg | Ratio |
306	|---------|---------|---------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|
307	| Qwen/Qwen3-8B | BF16 | - | 0.9136 | 0.7290 | 0.7671 | 0.5708 | 0.7451 | 100.00% |
308	| Qwen/Qwen3-8B | MXFP4 | - | 0.8560 | 0.6775 | 0.7323 | 0.5289 | 0.6987 | 93.77% |
309	| Qwen/Qwen3-8B | MXFP4 | R1 (online, 32) + R2 (offline) + R4 (online, 32) | 0.8575 | 0.7009 | 0.7595 | 0.5352 | 0.7133 | 95.73% |
310	
311	**Qwen3-32B** — rotation improves MXFP4 from 98.36% to 98.53% of BF16, recovering
312	most of the remaining PIQA and MMLU drop with R1 + R4 alone.
313	
314	| Model | Scheme | Rotation | GSM8K (strict, acc) | MMLU (acc) | PIQA (acc_norm) | HellaSwag (acc) | Avg | Ratio |
315	|---------|---------|---------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|
316	| Qwen/Qwen3-32B | BF16 | - | 0.9287 | 0.8076 | 0.8118 | 0.6389 | 0.7968 | 100.00% |
317	| Qwen/Qwen3-32B | MXFP4 | - | 0.9272 | 0.7876 | 0.7900 | 0.6300 | 0.7837 | 98.36% |
318	| Qwen/Qwen3-32B | MXFP4 | R1 (online, 32) + R4 (online, 32) | 0.9249 | 0.7908 | 0.8030 | 0.6215 | 0.7851 | 98.53% |
319	
320	**Qwen2.5-72B** — rotation improves MXFP4 from 97.60% to 98.58% of BF16 (+0.98 pts),
321	with gains across every task.
322	
323	| Model | Scheme | Rotation | GSM8K (strict, acc) | MMLU (acc) | PIQA (acc_norm) | HellaSwag (acc) | Avg | Ratio |
324	|---------|---------|---------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|
325	| Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B | BF16 | - | 0.9454 | 0.8346 | 0.8335 | 0.7035 | 0.8293 | 100.00% |
326	| Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B | MXFP4 | - | 0.9242 | 0.8104 | 0.8226 | 0.6803 | 0.8094 | 97.60% |
327	| Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B | MXFP4 | R1 (online, 32) + R4 (online, 32) | 0.9333 | 0.8204 | 0.8292 | 0.6871 | 0.8175 | 98.58% |
328	
329	> **Note:** Exact numbers depend on the model, task set, lm-eval version and hardware.
330	> Treat these as illustrative of the *trend* — rotation improving low-bit accuracy —
331	> rather than as guaranteed values.

102	def normalize_rotation_config(
103	    config: Any,
104	) -> BaseRotationConfig | None:
105	    """Normalise any supported config form to the canonical :class:`BaseRotationConfig` subclass.
106	
107	    Dispatches by inspecting the ``algorithm`` field (or missing field for
108	    legacy dicts that only carry Hadamard keys).
109	
110	    Args:
111	        config: One of: ``None``, :class:`RotationConfig`, a ``dict`` with
112	                an ``"algorithm"`` key, or a plain Hadamard shorthand string
113	                (including ``"quarot"`` / ``"spinquant"``).
114	
115	    Returns:
116	        The appropriate :class:`BaseRotationConfig` subclass, or ``None``
117	        when *config* is ``None`` / empty.
118	    """
119	    if config is None:
120	        return None
121	
122	    if isinstance(config, BaseRotationConfig):
123	        return config
124	
125	    if isinstance(config, dict):
126	        alg = config.get("algorithm", "hadamard")
127	        if alg == "hadamard":
128	            return RotationConfig.model_validate(config)
129	        if alg == "spinquant":
130	            from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.spinquant.preprocessor import SpinQuantConfig
131	
132	            # Filter to only valid SpinQuantConfig fields
133	            import dataclasses
134	
135	            valid_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(SpinQuantConfig)}
136	            filtered = {k: v for k, v in config.items() if k != "algorithm" and k in valid_fields}
137	            return SpinQuantConfig(**filtered)
138	        raise ValueError(
139	            f"Unknown rotation algorithm: {alg!r}. " f"Registered algorithms: {sorted(BaseRotation._REGISTRY)}"
140	        )
141	
142	    if isinstance(config, str):
143	        key = config.strip().lower()
144	        if key in ("spinquant", "quarot"):
145	            from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.spinquant.preprocessor import SpinQuantConfig
146	
147	            # "quarot" → QuaRot defaults (fixed Hadamard, no training)
148	            if key == "quarot":
149	                return SpinQuantConfig(trainable_rotation=False, trainable_smooth=False)
150	            # "spinquant" → experimental trainable mode
151	            return SpinQuantConfig(trainable_rotation=True, trainable_smooth=True)
152	        # Otherwise treat as Hadamard config.
153	        return RotationConfig.model_validate(_normalize_hadamard_config(config))
154	
155	    raise TypeError(

165	    **kwargs: Any,
166	) -> torch.nn.Module:
167	    """Apply a rotation/transform algorithm to *model*.
168	
169	    This is the single, algorithm-agnostic entry point.  The correct
170	    :class:`BaseRotation` subclass is selected automatically from *config*.
171	
172	    Args:
173	        model:            Model to transform (modified in-place).
174	        config:           Rotation configuration.  Accepts:
175	
176	                          * ``None`` – no-op, returns *model* unmodified.
177	                          * :class:`RotationConfig` or compatible ``dict``/``str``.
178	                          * Any :class:`BaseRotationConfig` subclass.

306	def preregister_rotation_buffers(
307	    model: torch.nn.Module,
308	    quantization_config,
309	) -> int:
310	    """Pre-register empty rotation buffers before state_dict loading.
311	
312	    Extracts the rotation config dict from *quantization_config* by
313	    checking each registered :class:`SerializerMixin`'s
314	    :meth:`config_key` (e.g. ``"spinquant_config"``).
315	
316	    Note: does NOT use ``"rotation_config"`` — that key is reserved for
317	    the existing Hadamard rotation system with a different schema.
318	
319	    Returns the number of modules that received buffers, or 0 if
320	    no rotation config was found.
321	    """
322	    # Extract rotation config dict by checking registered serializer keys
323	    rotation_cfg = None
324	    _ensure_registry_populated()
325	
326	    if isinstance(quantization_config, dict):
327	        for _name, _cls in BaseRotation._REGISTRY.items():
328	            if not (isinstance(_cls, type) and issubclass(_cls, SerializerMixin)):
329	                continue
330	            try:
331	                legacy_key = _cls.config_key()
332	            except Exception:
333	                continue
334	            rotation_cfg = quantization_config.get(legacy_key)
335	            if rotation_cfg is not None:
336	                rotation_cfg = dict(rotation_cfg)
337	                rotation_cfg.setdefault("algorithm", _name)
338	                break
339	    else:
340	        # Object-style quantization_config (e.g. QuantizationConfig)
341	        # Check each registered serializer's config_key as attribute
342	        for _name, _cls in BaseRotation._REGISTRY.items():
343	            if not (isinstance(_cls, type) and issubclass(_cls, SerializerMixin)):
344	                continue
345	            try:
346	                legacy_key = _cls.config_key()
347	            except Exception:
348	                continue
349	            rotation_cfg = getattr(quantization_config, legacy_key, None)
350	            if rotation_cfg is not None:
351	                if isinstance(rotation_cfg, dict):
352	                    rotation_cfg = dict(rotation_cfg)
353	                    rotation_cfg.setdefault("algorithm", _name)

356	    if not rotation_cfg:

8	"""Unified entry point for Hadamard rotation/transform.
9	
10	Two backend implementations exist:
11	
12	* ``inplace``  – :mod:`auto_round.algorithms.transforms.hadamard.inplace`
13	    QuaRot-style residual-stream rotation. Works for any weight/activation
14	    dtype. Optionally fuses the online Hadamard into weights
15	    (``fuse_online_to_weight=True``).
16	* ``transform`` – :mod:`auto_round.algorithms.transforms.hadamard`
17	    Per-Linear weight + activation Hadamard with a fused triton kernel.
18	    Only supports MXFP4 / NVFP4 and **cannot** fuse online to weight.
19	
20	Routing is controlled by :class:`RotationConfig.backend`:
21	
22	    "inplace"    -> always inplace
23	    "transform"  -> always transform (validates dtype + no-fuse)
24	    "auto"       -> if user asked to fuse              -> inplace
25	                    elif data_type is mx_fp / nv_fp    -> transform
26	                    else                                -> inplace
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	from typing import Any, Union
32	
33	import torch
34	
35	import auto_round.envs as envs
36	from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.hadamard.config import RotationConfig, normalize_rotation_config
37	from auto_round.compressors.utils import is_mx_fp, is_nv_fp
38	from auto_round.utils import logger
39	
40	__all__ = ["apply_hadamard_rotation", "resolve_hadamard_backend"]

43	def _to_config(
44	    rotation_config: Union[str, dict, RotationConfig, None],
45	    data_type: str,
46	) -> RotationConfig:
47	    """Normalise *rotation_config* and return a :class:`RotationConfig` instance."""
48	    cfg_dict = normalize_rotation_config(rotation_config, data_type)
49	    if isinstance(cfg_dict, RotationConfig):
50	        return cfg_dict
51	    return RotationConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict or {})

54	def resolve_hadamard_backend(config: RotationConfig, data_type: str) -> str:
55	    """Resolve the actual backend (``"inplace"`` / ``"transform"``) from config."""
56	    requested = config.backend
57	    fuse_requested = bool(config.fuse_online_to_weight)
58	    allow_online_rotation: bool = config.allow_online_rotation
59	
60	    if requested == "inplace" or "inplace" in config.hadamard_type:
61	        config.hadamard_type = config.hadamard_type[len("inplace_") :]
62	        return "inplace"
63	
64	    transform_backend_name = "transform"
65	    if requested == "transform":
66	        if fuse_requested:
67	            raise ValueError(
68	                f"backend='{transform_backend_name}' does not support fuse_online_to_weight=True. "
69	                "Use backend='inplace' (or backend='auto' with fuse_online_to_weight=True) instead."
70	            )
71	        if not (is_mx_fp(data_type) or is_nv_fp(data_type)):
72	            raise ValueError(
73	                f"backend='{transform_backend_name}' only supports MXFP4 / NVFP4 (got data_type={data_type!r}). "
74	                "Use backend='inplace' or backend='auto' for other dtypes."
75	            )
76	        if not allow_online_rotation:
77	            raise ValueError(f"backend='{transform_backend_name}' only supports `allow_online_rotation`=True")
78	
79	        return "transform"
80	
81	    # backend == "auto"
82	    if fuse_requested:
83	        return "inplace"
84	    if is_mx_fp(data_type) or is_nv_fp(data_type):
85	        return "transform"
86	    return "inplace"

89	def apply_hadamard_rotation(
90	    model: torch.nn.Module,
91	    rotation_config: Union[str, dict, RotationConfig, None],
92	    data_type: str,
93	    compute_device: torch.device | str = None,
94	) -> (torch.nn.Module, Any):
95	    """Apply Hadamard rotation/transform to *model*, dispatching by backend.
96	
97	    Args:
98	        model: Target model.
99	        rotation_config: ``str`` / ``dict`` / :class:`RotationConfig` / ``None``.
100	            See :class:`RotationConfig` for fields.
101	        data_type: Quantization data type (e.g. ``"mx_fp"``, ``"nv_fp"``,
102	            ``"int"``, ``"fp"``).
103	        compute_device: Device for inplace-backend computation. Ignored by
104	            the transform backend.
105	
106	    Returns:
107	        The same model (for chaining); also stored on ``model._rotation_config``.
108	    """
109	    config = _to_config(rotation_config, data_type)
110	    backend = resolve_hadamard_backend(config, data_type)
111	
112	    # Resolve fuse flag: explicit > env var > default(True)
113	    fuse_online_to_weight = config.fuse_online_to_weight
114	    if config.fuse_online_to_weight is not None:
115	        fuse_online_to_weight = bool(config.fuse_online_to_weight)
116	    elif envs.AR_FUSE_ONLINE_ROTATION:
117	        fuse_online_to_weight = bool(envs.AR_FUSE_ONLINE_ROTATION)
118	
119	    logger.info(
120	        f"Applying Hadamard (backend={backend}, "
121	        f"data_type={data_type}, fuse_online_to_weight={fuse_online_to_weight if backend == 'inplace' else False})."
122	    )
123	
124	    if backend == "inplace":
125	        logger.warning("this backend does not support real exporting, please export the model to fake format")
126	        from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.hadamard.inplace import apply_rotation_transform
127	
128	        # block_size -> group_size (None / -1 / 0 means full-dimension)
129	        bs = config.block_size
130	        group_size = bs if (bs is not None and bs > 0) else None
131	
132	        model, hooks = apply_rotation_transform(
133	            model,
134	            group_size=group_size,
135	            allow_online_rotation=config.allow_online_rotation,
136	            rotation_matrix=config.hadamard_type,
137	            fuse_online_to_weight=fuse_online_to_weight,
138	            compute_device=compute_device,
139	        )
140	        # Stash config object for downstream (export / serialization).
141	        setattr(model, "_rotation_config", config)
142	        return model, hooks
143	
144	    elif backend == "transform":
145	        supported_hadamard_types = ("hadamard", "random_hadamard")
146	        if config.hadamard_type not in supported_hadamard_types:
147	            raise ValueError("this backend only supports hadamard or random_hadamard")
148	        from auto_round.algorithms.transforms.hadamard.apply import apply_rotation_transform
149	
150	        return apply_rotation_transform(model, config, data_type=data_type)
151	    else:
152	        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported Hadamard backend {backend!r}")
